title: Finite tangent and infinitesimal automorphism spaces of curves
statement: On schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $\mathcal C(T)$ be the groupoid of flat proper finitely presented morphisms $X\to T$ of algebraic spaces whose geometric fibres have dimension at most one [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Arrows in $\mathcal C(T)$ are $T$-isomorphisms and pullback is cartesian base change; arrows over $T'\to T$ are isomorphisms $X'\cong X\times_TT'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Algebraic spaces are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Flatness and local finite presentation for their morphisms are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is proper if it is separated, of finite type and universally closed: separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion, finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale charts, and universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (the scheme conventions are [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). Let $K$ be any field [def-weil-field] and $x=(X\to\operatorname{Spec}K)\in\mathcal C(K)$. The isomorphism classes of objects in $\mathcal C(K[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))$ with a chosen identification of special fibre with $X$ form the tangent $K$-vector space $T_x$, and the automorphisms of the trivial deformation $X\times_K\operatorname{Spec}(K[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))$ which restrict to the identity on $X$ form the infinitesimal automorphism $K$-vector space $\operatorname{Inf}_x$. Both vector spaces are finite-dimensional. The vector operations are the usual deformation operations: pullback by $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$ gives scalar multiplication and the addition map on square-zero directions gives addition.

proof.text: For $M=K$, the split square-zero algebra $K\oplus K$ is $K[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ via $(a,b)\mapsto a+b\epsilon$; its square-zero ideal is $K\epsilon\cong K$. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-space-split-deformation-ext] to the flat algebraic space $X/K$. With the trivial deformation as zero, the vector space $V$ of all marked flat deformations of $X$ over the dual numbers is identified with $\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathrm{NL}_{X/K},\mathcal O_X)$, since $\mathcal O_X\otimes_KK\cong\mathcal O_X$. The group of automorphisms of the trivial deformation reducing to the identity is likewise identified with $\operatorname{Ext}^0(\mathrm{NL}_{X/K},\mathcal O_X)$. The identifications respect scalar pullback and square-zero addition.

source.place: Tag 0D1K (lemma-spaces-tangent-space), displayed Ext formulas, via defos.tex Tag 0D17.

proof.text: Forgetting properness, finite presentation, and the fibre-dimension condition includes the marked curve-deformation groupoid as a full subgroupoid of the marked flat-deformation groupoid. Indeed, in both categories arrows are all isomorphisms over the same base respecting the same marking. Consequently it induces an injection $j:T_x\hookrightarrow V$ on isomorphism classes. Both groupoids contain the trivial deformation, so $j$ preserves zero. The infinitesimal automorphism group in the item is exactly the ambient infinitesimal automorphism group: the object is the same trivial family and both arrow definitions impose precisely the same conditions.

The curve operations remain in the image of $j$. Put $D=\operatorname{Spec}(K[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))$. For two marked curve deformations over $D$, their markings give gluing data over $\operatorname{Spec}K$. By [lem-sfb-curve-infinitesimal-pushout] these glue in $\mathcal C$ over $P=D\amalg_{\operatorname{Spec}K}D$. Its ring is $K[\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2]/(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)^2$: explicitly it is the fibre product of two copies of $K[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ over $K$. Pulling this family back along $D\to P$ with both $\epsilon_i\mapsto\epsilon$ gives their sum in $\mathcal C(D)$. Scalar pullback $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$ also belongs to $\mathcal C(D)$ by its specified base-change functor. Forgetting to flat deformations performs these identical gluing and pullback operations, so [lem-sfb-flat-space-split-deformation-ext] gives $j(u+v)=j(u)+j(v)$ and $j(au)=a\,j(u)$. In particular $a=-1$ supplies additive inverses. The image is a vector subspace of $V$; injectivity transfers every vector-space identity to $T_x$. For infinitesimal automorphisms the same cited Ext identification already gives the vector structure, with composition as addition. This also proves that the structures just obtained are the deformation operations specified in the statement.

proof.text: A field is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $0$ and $K$. The structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is locally of finite presentation because it is finitely presented by hypothesis. Apply [lem-sfb-space-naive-cotangent-coherent] to obtain that $X$ is locally Noetherian, that $\mathcal O_X$ is coherent, and that $\mathrm{NL}_{X/K}$ has coherent cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$. Thus $E=\mathrm{NL}_{X/K}$ has coherent cohomology bounded above and $F=\mathcal O_X[0]$ has coherent cohomology bounded below.

Use the properness of $X/K$ and the bounds from step 4 in [lem-sfb-proper-space-coherent-ext-finite], with $A=K$, $E=\mathrm{NL}_{X/K}$, $F=\mathcal O_X[0]$, and $n=0,1$. Both displayed Ext groups are finitely generated $K$-modules, hence finite-dimensional vector spaces. In particular $V$ is finite-dimensional, and so is the infinitesimal automorphism space under the identification of step 1.

source.place: Tag 0D1K (lemma-spaces-tangent-space), final application of spaces-perfect.tex Tag 0D0T.

proof.text: Let $d=\dim_KV<\infty$. Any $d+1$ elements of $T_x$ have linearly dependent images in $V$. Since $j$ is linear and injective, a nontrivial linear relation between those images gives the same nontrivial relation in $T_x$. Starting with the empty independent list and adjoining a vector outside the current span must therefore stop after at most $d$ choices, yielding a finite basis of $T_x$. Together with step 5 this proves both finiteness assertions. The argument applies to every field $K$, and consequently also to fields of finite type over $\mathbf Z$.

lean.statement: theorem finite_tangent_and_infinitesimalAut {S : Scheme.{u}} (K : Type u) [Field K] (a : Spec (.of K) ⟶ S) (X : ProperCurveFamily (Over.mk a)) : ∃ (tadd : AddCommGroup (Tangent X)) (tmod : @Module K (Tangent X) _ tadd.toAddCommMonoid) (iadd : AddCommGroup (InfinitesimalAut X)) (imod : @Module K (InfinitesimalAut X) _ iadd.toAddCommMonoid), @FiniteDimensional K (Tangent X) _ tadd tmod ∧ @FiniteDimensional K (InfinitesimalAut X) _ iadd imod ∧ (∀ t : Tangent X, IsTangentZero X t ↔ t = tadd.zero) ∧ (∀ t s r : Tangent X, IsTangentAdd X t s r ↔ r = tadd.add t s) ∧ (∀ (c : K) (t s : Tangent X), IsTangentSMul X c t s ↔ s = tmod.smul c t) ∧ iadd.zero.val = Iso.refl _ ∧ (∀ α β : InfinitesimalAut X, (iadd.add α β).val.hom = α.val.hom ≫ β.val.hom) ∧ (∀ (c : K) (α β : InfinitesimalAut X), IsInfinitesimalAutSMul X c α β ↔ β = imod.smul c α)
